title: Prove no toggle alphabet beats the five-source connector DUO point (no κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. No κ change.** This answers the open question of #3321: can two Q5 calls, or a mixed Q5/DUO/TRIO alphabet, create a new priced point on the five-source, 31-row connector batch?

In the #943/#3321 interface, with every nonempty source subset available as one complete call (one dispatch plus `|S|` source additions, no surcharge):

- **Theorem 1.** Every correct schedule, over any toggle alphabet and any number of uses, has at least 72 queries and at least 74 additions. The DUO word of #1531 attains both, so the minimum price is `72o + 74p` for all `o >= 0`, `p > 0`, and `(72, 74)` is the only Pareto point. No mixture and no number of Q5 calls improves it.
- **Theorem 2.** Every schedule that contains a weight-5 call has at least 78 additions, so its price is at least `72o + 78p`, the DUO price plus `4p`. The bound is attained by a word with one Q5, two DUOs and seven singletons (ten calls, 16 additions). Two or more Q5 calls give at least 80 additions.

So a mixed Q5/DUO alphabet does give a priced point that beats the singleton witness `(74, 74)`, exactly when `o > 2p`. No alphabet beats the DUO point at any price. With a per-multi-source-call surcharge `sigma`, the DUO word wins over singletons exactly when `sigma < o`, and the Q5 word is dominated for every `sigma >= 0`.

New here: the partial-coverage form of the support bound (`T + 2u >= 10`, where `u` counts rows no boundary pair realizes), the expansion bound `A >= 74` for every alphabet, the single-point frontier, the weight-5 floor 78 and its attaining word. The full-coverage support bound for steps of weight 1 to 5 is #4137. The 945-pairing census and singleton minimum are #943, the DUO word and the 99,200 ten-point covers are #1531, and the Q5 model and one-Q5 census are #3321. These are cited inputs, recomputed as controls, not audited.

## Evidence and reproduction

Interpreter: `/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`. Any CPython 3.12 works; only the standard library is used. From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/five-source-toggle-frontier/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/five-source-toggle-frontier/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/five-source-toggle-frontier
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/five-source-toggle-frontier --check-source-history
```

Run locally at head `7ef416e83b8220d0a2f91cb34ea0c3bb9d892154`: both verifier modes pass in about 17 s each (`PASS_FIVE_SOURCE_TOGGLE_FRONTIER nine_point_covers=0 ten_point_covers=99200 ... weight5_witness=(72,78) no_new_kappa`), the package runner prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/five-source-toggle-frontier outcome=negative-result` in 33 s, `--check-only` prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`, and the commit check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

The verifier recomputes from integers:

- no nine-point set of `F_2^5` has `P + P = F_2^5` (exhaustive search with an exact waste cut, and the affine-basis normal form); the same search finds 99,200 ten-point covers, the count recorded by `research/duo-toggle-connector`;
- the 945 length-ten pairing words (coverage histogram equal to #943's, best 31 of 32 masks);
- the 115,920 closed words with one weight-5 step and nine singletons (at most 27 of 31 differences);
- the DUO and weight-5 words as explicit 72-call schedules, each replayed symbolically for arbitrary operators and concretely with random binary maps and dirty data;
- the `T + 2u` table, the Theorem 2 case checks for `T <= 40`, 30,000 random closed words over all 31 toggles, a 6,000-step hill climb, and nine rejection controls.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- The price model is the favorable ledger of #3321: a multi-source call costs one dispatch plus its additions, with no frame, routing or implementation surcharge. No physical call, compiler or supplier is established.
- The model is the binary-linear five-source, 31-row interface with singleton readouts. Joint readouts, extra connectors, mutable sources, frame changes and other source counts are outside it.
- The reduction to prefix differences is inherited from #943 (necessity by the identity-map specialization). The proofs are written; finite components are exhaustive under the stated reductions. No proof assistant was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
- Weights 3 and 4 have no analogue of Theorem 2 here.
- Verifier discipline: no recursion and a finite bound on every loop; the cover search enforces a 60,000,000-step limit against the 5,403,753 and 41,511,450 steps it uses. Python allocates integers and containers while it runs, a managed-runtime deviation confined to these bounded searches.

## Open next questions

1. Exact minimum price among schedules containing a weight-3 or weight-4 call. First step: rerun the depth-first search used for the Q5 witness with one such call and extra weight 2 to 6. Nothing blocks it.
2. Does the single-point collapse hold for every alphabet at six sources? #2249 reports `r((C2)^6) = 14` and `f(6) = 16`, which would give `(140, 142)`. First step: rerun the support and expansion arguments with those invariants. The invariants are cited from an unmerged package.
3. Can a readout-side alphabet move the 62-readout floor (62 of the 72 queries)? Toggle-side extensions cannot. Blocked: no priced joint-readout call is defined.

## Related open work

- #2249 studies the six-source analogue (general-arity toggle floor). It uses the same support-plus-expansion idea at six sources; this PR computes only the five-source numbers, so there is no shared figure to compare.
- #3909 bounds the five-source arity-four extension at 149 units against 148 for singletons. This PR's alphabet-agnostic floor is 146 units (72 + 74), attained by DUO, so the two are consistent.
- #2134 is a six-source one-TRIO census, a different source count.
- #3897 studies a joint-output readout, the readout side that open question 3 leaves open; this PR does not touch it.
- #3919 audits a direct-call interface boundary; it does not study the toggle ledger.
- #4079 bounds seven-source connectors of weight at most four, a different source count.
- #6696 (same author) studies the eight-query mutable-source tariff, a different connector interface (common-B mutable-source words). This PR computes no figure that it also computes.

## CI notes

CI did not certify this result. The `plan` job of [run 41721283470](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41721283470) at head `7ef416e83b8220d0a2f91cb34ea0c3bb9d892154` ([job 126214604601](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41721283470/job/126214604601)) was cancelled by the workflow's 10-minute timeout while still in the `actions/checkout` step (21:23:22Z to 21:33:26Z). The `replay` job was skipped, so no package step ran in CI. The package did not cause this.

Checked on other PRs: the `plan` job of #6676, #6691 and #6692 was cancelled at the same `actions/checkout` step after about 10 minutes. Of the 19 PRs numbered 6676 to 6696 whose checks I read, 13 show a `plan` failure of about 10 minutes and 6 passed.

The result is certified only by the local checks listed under Evidence and reproduction (both verifier modes, the registered package runner, the metadata check and the commit-byte check, all at head `7ef416e83b8220d0a2f91cb34ea0c3bb9d892154`).
